:::{#lem-partial-pooling-blp}
#### The partial-pooling weight minimizes mean squared error

In the random-intercept model with known $\mu$, $\sigma_\alpha^2$, and $\sigma^2$,
consider predictors of the group mean $\mu_j \eqdef \mu + \alpha_j$ of the form

$$
\tilde\mu_j(c) \eqdef \mu + c\,(\bar{y}_j - \mu)
$$

for a constant $c$.
The mean squared error $\E{\paren{\tilde\mu_j(c) - \mu_j}^2}$ is minimized at $c = w_j$,
the weight in @eq-partial-pooling,
which can also be written as

$$
w_j = \frac{\sigma_\alpha^2}{\sigma_\alpha^2 + \sigma^2 / n_j}.
$$ {#eq-partial-pooling-weight}

This result does not need the normality assumptions of the model,
only the means, variances, and independence of its terms.
:::
